title: High-to-Low Row Machine
summary: A plate-loaded row on a diagonal from above your head down to your waist, sitting between the High Row and a seated row and biased toward the lats.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.8 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.5 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.35 for rear delts (minor): each working set adds 0.35 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.

setup.text: Sit with your chest on the pad and reach up and forward for the handles.
Pull down and back on the diagonal until your elbows reach your hips.
Return slowly until your lats stretch.

form_cues.cue: Drive the elbows toward your hips
Drive your elbows toward your back pockets.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders as you pull.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.
